Subject: Clarification on SLA coverage for Private VPC (customer-managed edge)

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the deployment last week — our Private deployment on the us-west-2 host is live and serving traffic. We surfaced a couple of customer questions this morning that I wanted to get aligned on before we close the onboarding checklist.

Issue summary: last night we had two short incidents where end-to-end latency spiked (p95 stayed fine, but p99.9 and p100 showed ~600-800ms tails) for a subset of requests. Our preliminary posteriori traces show the tokenization + Redwood runtime step is within normal bounds; the tail appears to correlate with the customer-controlled NAT/edge transit in our colo (we run our own firewall/egress appliance).

Silverpine is asking whether Redwood will recognize a limited SLA carveout/exception for latency/outage attribution that can be directly tied to customer-managed network infrastructure. Specifically they want: 1) clear language to include as an addendum to the SOW that avoids Redwood penalties where the root cause is customer-managed transit; and 2) a list of evidence/artifacts Redwood will accept when we request an exception.

I have attached a quick traceroute sample and our high-level network diagram to help diagnose. Can you advise on what we should collect and what the typical addendum language looks like? We want something that is operationally simple (not a months-long debate) but defensible for both sides.

Attachments: traceroute-output-20280717.txt, network-diagram-vpc.png

Appreciate any guidance — we need to turn around a requested change for our procurement team by EOD Thursday (US).

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Platform Operations
Silverpine Health

Subject: Re: Clarification on SLA coverage for Private VPC (customer-managed edge)

Thanks Lena — and congrats on the launch. I dug into the traceroute you attached and agree it points to elevated egress latency at your colo boundary during the windows you flagged. We can support a limited SLA attribution carveout for customer-managed network egress, but to keep it operationally straightforward we need two things up front:

1) A short, objective evidence checklist Silverpine will produce when requesting an exception. Typical items we accept:
  - synchronized traceroute/mtr (with timestamps and hop delays) covering the incident window
  - tcpdump/pcap excerpt or flow logs showing packet retransmits or drops originating at the customer egress
  - a diagram showing the exact path (your network-diagram-vpc.png is helpful) and the appliance/make/model responsible for egress
  - confirmation of config changes/maintenance windows if any

2) Instrumentation access or forwarding of specific telemetry for the incident window (sftp/secure-share of logs or a temporary telemetry-forwarding agreement). We don't need full access permanently — just enough to independently validate the causal boundary.

Proposed contractual language (draft):
"Redwood's availability and latency commitments do not apply to failures or degradations caused solely by Customer-managed network infrastructure (including but not limited to customer-provisioned NATs, firewalls, and colo egress appliances). For an exception to apply, Customer must provide concurrent evidence (traceroute, packet captures/flow logs, and a network topology diagram) demonstrating the fault lies outside Redwood-managed infrastructure. Upon review, Redwood will determine whether the incident qualifies for attribution to Customer infrastructure and, if so, exclude the incident from SLA calculations."

Operational suggestion: we can offer a one-page exception addendum that references the checklist above and specifies acceptable evidence formats. If you want, I can draft that addendum and share with legal/your contracts team for a quick redline.

Next steps from our side: Vivek and Karthik — can you confirm the minimum telemetry formats we can consume for rapid validation? Naomi — if this looks OK I'll draft the addendum and circulate.

Jasmine Liu
Solutions Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Jul 18, 2028 at 11:03 AM jasmine_liu@redwood.ai wrote:
> Proposed contractual language (draft):
> "Redwood's availability and latency commitments do not apply to failures or degradations caused solely by Customer-managed network infrastructure..."

High-level technical checklist (we agree with the proposed approach). A few specifics to speed adjudication and keep false positives low:

- Required evidence window: traceroute/mtr and tcpdump samples must include timestamps in UTC and cover the full incident window +/- 60s.
- Acceptable traceroute: ICMP or UDP-based traceroutes are fine; we prefer results that show increasing latency or packet loss starting at a specific hop inside customer-managed gear.
- Packet capture: 30s-120s pcap around the incident start is usually sufficient; highlight retransmits and RTOs. If PCAP can't be shared, NetFlow/Flow logs with byte/packet counts and retransmit indicators are acceptable.
- Thresholds for automated acceptance (ops fast-path): if customer evidence shows >2% packet loss or >250ms median RTT increase at the egress hop affecting >5% of sampled connections during the window, ops will preliminarily attribute to customer infra and exclude from SLA pending final review.
- If evidence is borderline, we'll open a 48-hour validation window where both teams share telemetry and run joint traces.

We can produce a short template evidence bundle and a small validation script that parses traceroutes/pcaps to extract the key indicators. I will attach a one-page ops checklist to this thread (ops-checklist-v1.txt) for your team to use.

Vivek Kulkarni
Engineering, Runtime Ops
Redwood Inference
